description: Authoritative license compatibility matrix for top 20 open source licenses covering ~95% of packages
methodology: Based on FSF GPL Compatibility List, Mozilla MPL FAQ, Apache Foundation guidance, and SPDX specifications

MIT.description: Highly permissive license with minimal restrictions

sources.citation: FSF: MIT license is permissive and GPL-compatible

MIT.reasoning: Permissive licenses cannot incorporate copyleft-licensed code without violating copyleft requirements

Apache-2.0.description: Permissive license with explicit patent grant

sources.citation: Apache 2.0 patent clause incompatible with GPL-2.0, but compatible with GPL-3.0

Apache-2.0.reasoning: Apache 2.0's patent grant conflicts with GPLv2 section 6, but GPLv3 was designed to resolve this

sources.citation: FSF: 3-clause BSD is permissive and GPL-compatible

BSD-3-Clause.reasoning: Permissive license, same reasoning as MIT

sources.citation: FSF: 2-clause BSD is permissive and GPL-compatible
FSF: ISC license is permissive and GPL-compatible

ISC.reasoning: Permissive license, same reasoning as MIT

sources.citation: FSF: 0BSD is ultra-permissive public domain equivalent

0BSD.reasoning: Public domain equivalent - compatible with everything

sources.citation: FSF: GPL-3.0 is compatible with LGPL (via Section 3 upgrade), Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0

GPL-3.0-only.reasoning: Strong copyleft - requires all combined code to be GPL-3.0. LGPL can upgrade to GPL (Section 3). MPL 2.0 Section 3.3 allows GPL combination. Apache-2.0 patent clause resolved in GPLv3.

GPL-3.0-or-later.description: GNU General Public License v3.0 or any later version

sources.citation: FSF: GPL-3.0-or-later provides upgrade path flexibility

GPL-3.0-or-later.reasoning: Same as GPL-3.0-only but with upgrade flexibility

sources.citation: FSF: GPL-2.0 incompatible with Apache-2.0 (patent clause), MPL-2.0, and GPL-3.0

GPL-2.0-only.reasoning: Strong copyleft. Incompatible with Apache-2.0 (patent clause conflict), MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft incompatibility), and GPL-3.0 (different copyleft terms)

GPL-2.0-or-later.description: GNU General Public License v2.0 or any later version

sources.citation: FSF: GPL-2.0-or-later can upgrade to GPL-3.0, resolving compatibility issues

GPL-2.0-or-later.reasoning: Upgrade path to GPL-3.0 resolves Apache-2.0 and MPL-2.0 incompatibilities

LGPL-2.1-only.description: GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1

sources.citation: LGPL Section 3: Can upgrade to corresponding GPL version

LGPL-2.1-only.reasoning: Weak copyleft - Section 3 allows upgrading to GPL. Incompatible with Apache-2.0 due to GPLv2 patent clause conflict.

LGPL-2.1-or-later.description: GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1 or any later version

sources.citation: LGPL Section 3: Upgrade path to GPL resolves incompatibilities

LGPL-2.1-or-later.reasoning: Can upgrade to LGPL-3.0 or GPL-3.0, resolving Apache-2.0 incompatibility

LGPL-3.0-only.description: GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0

sources.citation: LGPL-3.0 Section 3: Can upgrade to GPL-3.0

LGPL-3.0-only.reasoning: Weak copyleft with GPL upgrade path. Compatible with Apache-2.0 and MPL-2.0 via GPL-3.0 upgrade.

LGPL-3.0-or-later.description: GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0 or any later version

sources.citation: LGPL-3.0-or-later provides upgrade flexibility

LGPL-3.0-or-later.reasoning: Same as LGPL-3.0-only but with upgrade flexibility

sources.citation: MPL 2.0 Section 3.3: Secondary licenses allow GPL combination

MPL-2.0.reasoning: Section 3.3 allows MPL-2.0 code to be relicensed under GPL/LGPL when combined. Incompatible with GPL-2.0-only due to terms conflict.

AGPL-3.0-only.description: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (network use = distribution)

sources.citation: FSF: AGPL-3.0 incompatible with GPL (stricter terms)

AGPL-3.0-only.reasoning: Network copyleft - stricter than GPL. Cannot combine AGPL with GPL due to additional restrictions.

AGPL-3.0-or-later.description: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or any later version

sources.citation: FSF: AGPL-3.0-or-later incompatible with GPL
Public domain dedication - no restrictions
Public domain waiver - no restrictions

CC0-1.0.reasoning: Public domain waiver - compatible with everything

WTFPL.description: Do What The F*ck You Want To Public License

sources.citation: Ultra-permissive - no restrictions
